Engulf

en-GUHLF · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To engulf is to completely cover, surround, or swallow up.

A sense of grief seemed to engulf the entire town after the news of the accident spread.

Worked Example

The avalanche roared down the mountainside and engulfed the ski lodge in seconds, burying it completely under snow.

Engulf means to completely cover, surround, or swallow something up -- here, the lodge was totally buried by the avalanche.

How Engulf Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

envelop

envelop: to completely wrap or surround something

submerge

submerge: to completely cover with liquid; to sink below the surface

Antonyms

expose

expose: to uncover or leave unprotected, the opposite of engulfing

reveal

reveal: to make visible or known, the opposite of swallowing something up

How Strong Is It? — brush → engulf → consume

brush vs. engulf

brush vs. engulf: To brush something is to touch it only lightly along its edge, far less than fully engulfing it.

consume vs. engulf

consume vs. engulf: To consume, as fire or floodwater does, is to completely destroy through engulfing, an even more total and violent image than simply engulfing.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — en-

prefix — en-: to put into, to cause to be in (French/Latin)

root — gulf

root — gulf: a large hollow or chasm; a bay of the sea (Greek kolpos, via Old Italian golfo)

Put it together

Put it together: Engulf combines the prefix en- ('to put into') with the standalone English word gulf ('a large hollow, chasm, or bay'). To engulf something is literally to pull it into a gulf -- a huge, swallowing space -- which is exactly the image of something being completely covered or swallowed up.

Use the root in a new word: gulf

Use the root in a new word: gulf: The Gulf of Mexico is a large body of water partly enclosed by the coastlines of the United States, Mexico, and Cuba.

Word Choice

Engulf can describe something physical (flames, water, smoke) or something emotional (grief, fear, panic) that completely overtakes a person or place.
